Checkout now fetches the selected PR head branch using a branch-specific refspec and no longer follows it with the repository-wide unshallow pull that fetched the contributor's other branches. The fix shipped in v0.79.2024012510.
rows.verifyEvidence: The commit only removes depth-1 shallow fetches and the follow-up unshallow pull to fix unshallow errors. The fetch was already a targeted single-ref fetch before this change, so the commit does not stop the remote from fetching every branch.

rows.title: 'There are updates available for this pull request.' - Successfully merged PR is checked out?

This is now tracked by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-pull-request-github/issues/6711: reusing the same `dev` branch for successive pull requests can leave it associated with an older closed or merged PR. Your additional symptoms are useful context there—the stale association produces the repeated update notification, enters review mode for the merged PR, and can make Exit Review Mode switch from `dev` to `main`.
rows.verifyEvidence: gate: the cited canonical #6711 is closed — a duplicate close would strand the report (re-review, not close)

Your earlier VS Code 1.96.2 logs showing that no keybinding when-clause matched, while Ctrl+A/E/B still worked, are useful corroborating evidence for that investigation.

rows.title: Feature Request: Display verified commits label from GitHub in Pull Request viewer in VS Code

Please also include whether this is GitHub.com or GitHub Enterprise (and its version), the repository setup (single repository or fork with an upstream remote), and whether loading the key into the remote SSH agent changes the result. That should show which branch/PR detection operation is failing before the extension opens the separate read-only resource.

rows.title: Sticky PR/Issue headers when scrolling

It now appears after the normal PR or issue title scrolls out of view, retaining the status, title, item number, and copy-link action, so this request is resolved.
rows.verifyEvidence: Adds an IntersectionObserver-driven compressed header to the PR/issue overview, pinned at the top when the title scrolls off, with status, title, number and copy link. Leftover: no checkout/refresh actions in it.

This is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-pull-request-github/issues/4509, which covers both linking a branch created through “Start Working” to the issue’s Development section and offering an existing linked branch when starting work. Consolidating there; this report’s detail that a pushed extension-created branch remains absent from Development is part of the same request.
rows.verifyEvidence: B's second requirement asks that branches created via 'Start working on issue' be attached to the issue so they show under its Development section, which is exactly A's ask.

rows.title: Base branch for automatic branch creation when working on issues
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. This is now supported by the `githubIssues.workingBaseBranch` setting, added in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-pull-request-github/commit/8fa502f0a8d7bd08f2e699f0d923d259bbf78f84 and shipped in v0.126.0. It can create the issue branch from the current branch, switch to the repository default branch, or prompt between the two.
rows.verifyEvidence: Adds the githubIssues.workingBaseBranch setting (currentBranch default, defaultBranch, or prompt) and passes it to setCurrentIssue in place of the hardcoded true. Issue branches can now start from the current branch, one of the reporter's two options.

rows.title: Continuously trying to push changes (and fail)
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the detailed reproduction. In the Git state shown here, `stage-test` still tracks `github/master`; pushing `stage-test:stage-test` creates or updates the remote branch but does not change that tracking relationship. The extension relies on the configured upstream to determine whether commits are published, as explained in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-pull-request-github/issues/6978#issuecomment-3044408833. Using `git push --set-upstream github stage-test`, or running `git branch --set-upstream-to=github/stage-test stage-test` after the existing push, should make the branch report zero commits ahead and allow the creation flow to use the published branch.

rows.title: Bad Credentials issue is back with 0.148
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report and the version comparison. This is the same repeated authentication loop being tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-pull-request-github/issues/8786, so consolidating the investigation there. Carrying over the useful details from this report: Windows 11 Enterprise with VS Code 1.124.0, where extension 0.146 worked but 0.148 repeatedly prompted for authentication.
rows.verifyEvidence: Both were filed the same day and describe one regression in extension 0.148: it repeatedly asks the user to sign in to GitHub again. A notes 0.146 works fine; OS difference (Windows vs macOS) doesn't suggest a separate cause.

rows.title: Confirmation popup for the Cancel button of pull request creation
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. The confirmation before discarding unsaved pull request creation changes was implemented in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-pull-request-github/commit/e5245afc2f45b6c71a2145e30a1babc6d6079ecb and shipped in v0.162.0. Cancelling now prompts when the title, description, or other PR metadata has been changed, so this can be closed as completed.
rows.verifyEvidence: The cancel handler now opens a modal 'Discard' confirmation whenever the description or title has been edited, or metadata has been selected. Declining keeps the webview state, which covers the requested guard against an accidental Tab+Space cancel.
